description:
You are a data engineer preparing the environment for an ETL pipeline. Please list all currently installed Python packages from the active environment using pip and save the output into a file located at /home/user/etl_env/packages_list.txt. The output in /home/user/etl_env/packages_list.txt must include all installed packages and their versions, matching the format produced by the command pip list (i.e., the columns "Package" and "Version" should be separated by one or more spaces, and the first two lines must be headers and a row of dashes). For example, if only "numpy" and "pandas" were installed, the file would contain: 
Package    Version
---------- -------
numpy      1.24.3
pandas     2.0.2
Your task is complete when /home/user/etl_env/packages_list.txt contains the up-to-date list of all installed packages in this precise tabular format.
truth:
Directory /home/user/etl_env/ must exist before task begins, and user must have write permissions there.

The file /home/user/etl_env/packages_list.txt must exist after task completion. It must match exactly the output produced by running "pip list" in the current environment at the moment the agent completes the task, with all rows and headers in the correct fixed-width columns as pip formats by default. For instance, if the environment initially contains pip (version 23.0.1) and setuptools (version 65.5.0), the file contents must be:

Package    Version
---------- -------
pip        23.0.1
setuptools 65.5.0

The automated test will verify the presence of this file and check that its contents are a byte-for-byte match to the exact output of running "pip list" in the current environment.
